sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Browser Use is an open-source browser agent. You give it a task in plain English, and an AI model completes it in a real browser by writing Python that controls Chrome, such as finding information, filling forms or booking appointments.
sixtySeconds.problem: Automating websites with scripts breaks whenever pages change, and many tasks need judgement. Browser Use lets a model look at the page and decide what to do, so you can automate web tasks by describing them.
whoFor: Developers automating web tasks with AI
Coding agent users who want browser control
Teams running browser automation at scale
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a popular, Python-first browser agent that works with cloud browsers or your local Chrome, and with Browser Use's own model or your own LLM.
requirements: A Browser Use Cloud API key for the default setup, or your own model's API key
Chrome or Chromium for local browsers

overview: In version 1.0, the agent is a model plus a persistent Python REPL plus the Chrome DevTools Protocol: the model writes code cells that run against the browser and sees the output. It's built on Pydantic AI.

There are three ways to use it: the fully hosted cloud agent, a CLI you can hand to coding agents like Claude Code or Codex, or the Python library. By default the library uses the bu-4.0 model and a Browser Use Cloud browser with one key; you can instead drive a fresh local Chromium, your open Chrome with your logins, or a copy of a Chrome profile, with models such as ChatOpenAI, ChatAnthropic or ChatGoogle.

The README stresses pinning an exact version, because the project moves fast. It supports typed structured output and file uploads. Note that anyone with a cloud browser's live-view link can control it.

steps.title: Create a project and add Browser Use
steps.body: Pin the exact version, as the README advises.
steps.code:
uv init --python 3.12 my-agent && cd my-agent
uv add 'browser-use==1.0.8'

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Saves your Browser Use Cloud key. Over SSH use --device-code.

steps.title: Install
steps.code:
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install 'browser-use==1.0.8'
browser-use login

steps.title: Give this to your agent
steps.body: Paste the README's prompt into Claude Code, Codex or another agent; it installs the CLI and registers the skill.
steps.code:
uv tool install browser-use==1.0.8
browser-use skill install

firstRun.title: Run your first task
firstRun.code:
from browser_use import Agent

result = Agent('Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo').run_sync()
print(result.final_result())

tutorial.title: Run an agent on your own Chrome with your own model
tutorial.useCase: Drive a local Chromium with an OpenAI model instead of the cloud defaults.

steps.title: Write the script
steps.code:
from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatOpenAI

agent = Agent(
    'Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo',
    llm=ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna'),
    browser=Browser('chromium'),
)
print(agent.run_sync().final_result())

tutorial.expected: A fresh Chromium with a temporary profile opens, the agent browses to the repository and prints the star count.
nextSteps: Use Browser('chrome') to work with your logged-in Chrome
Try the hosted cloud agent to scale up
